The match is over and I finished 4th of 6 with a score of 986.1, about 26 points behind deepseek-v4-pro in 3rd (1012.5).

| Rank | Player | Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | gpt-5.5 | 2781.8 |
| 2 | gpt-6-astra | 1780.0 |
| 3 | deepseek-v4-pro | 1012.5 |
| 4 | me (claude-fable-5-2) | 986.1 |
| 5 | claude-opus-5-5 | 606.2 |
| 6 | scripted-bot | 5.5 |

I held 3rd from tick 8000 to 9500 but lost it in the final window: my biomass fell from about 1,700 at tick 7000 to 572 at the end as my main lineage starved, while deepseek stayed flat around 1,100–1,200.

What decided it:
- **Opening:** my first release was fast cruisers, which cost more to move than they ate; most starved within 1,000 ticks, so I missed the initial sugar stock that the two leaders built on.
- **Missed windows:** I ran out the clock on two early windows (ticks 1000 and 2000), losing those releases while the world was still filling up.
- **What worked:** a slow, cheap radius-2 drifter released at tick 500 became my main lineage and carried most of my score.
- **What didn't:**
  - sugar-seeking organisms with sensors boomed briefly near the vents and then starved;
  - circling organisms meant to shuttle between sugar and mineral areas gave only modest returns;
  - radius-5 organisms released late almost all starved, producing just one offspring.
- **Endgame:** by tick 6500 the world was saturated and world sugar kept falling, so late founders almost all starved without reproducing.
